summary: Wombat now runs queries on demand and exits when each request completes. Search work history, inspect usage and recheck improvements without retained views or a background service.
highlights: Run local CLI queries in the foreground. Installation no longer offers Wombat service startup or autostart options; internal SQLite indexes still support incremental collection and consistent accounting.

Read clear daily usage totals with compact JSON by default. Index-wide source warnings remain separate from the coverage of selected measurements, so unrelated historical warnings do not become unsupported claims about a selected date range.
Resolve complete conversation IDs directly and continue bounded source reads across unrelated index updates. Changed source evidence still fails explicitly rather than returning substituted text.

Save the original check or cleanup JSON report and supply it for verification. Rechecks preserve the original scope and rules across processes; cleanup continues to validate current ownership, physical identity, protected files and active consumers.
Cancel a rebuild without leaving its unpublished temporary index behind. Completed indexes, recovery copies, user decisions and original conversation records stay separate from temporary cleanup.
knownLimitations: This release removes public view selectors, saved-view operations and service controls without compatibility aliases. Update the runtime, plugin and automation together; use command --help --json or system api for current inputs.
If an older installation has resident startup enabled, stop it and remove its autostart registration with that version before upgrading. This release does not manage legacy service registrations.
Original reports are recheck baselines, not deletion permission or proof that conditions are unchanged. Missing, changed or incomplete evidence cannot establish a verified repair or justify cleanup.
First collection and expanded history queries can require waiting. No hard latency or memory ceiling is promised. Codex artifact cleanup remains limited to supported macOS layouts.

Local CLI analysis does not call models or upload conversations. Selected Skill evidence enters the current Codex conversation. Unknown source formats are rejected without migration or automatic data deletion.
